entries.title: P0017: October primary resolution claims require a current proof audit
entries.statement: As checked on 2026-10-10, P0017 asks for a universal C_P bound for all centered covariance-identity log-concave probabilities in every dimension, equivalently a universal positive Euclidean Cheeger lower bound. Its cited source is Randomstrasse101, arXiv:2603.29571v1, Entry 13, Conjecture 30. arXiv:2610.05474v1 (2026-10-04), Theorem 1.1, announces the full Poincare bound; arXiv:2610.07728v2 (2026-10-08 revision) announces C_P<=25. This card records primary announcements only: mathematical validity and current openness have not been independently settled in this packet. The September attempted-unsolved label is dated provenance, not a current-openness certificate.
assumptions: Source-status observation dated 2026-10-10; not a mathematical validation of the announced proofs.

entries.title: DRAFT: isotropic regular simplex has rare long conditional fibers
entries.statement: Unreviewed independent derivation: for n>=2 work on H={x in R^(n+1):sum x_i=0} with its Euclidean metric, and take X uniform on vertices v_i=sqrt((n+1)(n+2))(e_i-1/(n+1)). Covariance on H is identity. Put u=(e_0-e_1)/sqrt(2), T=<X,u>, Y=X-Tu and S=lambda_0+lambda_1 in barycentric coordinates. Conditional on Y, T is uniform on an interval of length sqrt(2(n+1)(n+2)) S, and S~Beta(2,n-1). Thus ess sup conditional C_P=2(n+1)(n+2)/pi^2, mean conditional C_P=12/pi^2, ess sup conditional variance=(n+1)(n+2)/6 and mean conditional variance=1. Cheeger uses boundary/min(mass,1-mass): ess inf conditional h=sqrt(2/((n+1)(n+2))). Near-extremal fibers have positive marginal probability: P(S>1-delta)=delta^(n-1)[n-(n-1)delta] for 0<delta<1. This blocks transferring global isotropy to a uniform conditional bound; it is not a KLS refutation or novelty claim.
assumptions: Euclidean metric on H; n>=2; orthogonal conditioning onto u-perp; marginal-almost-everywhere conditional laws.
C_P uses variance/Dirichlet energy; h uses boundary/min(mass,1-mass).
Independent referee check pending; proof in ATTEMPT.md sections 2-4.

entries.title: DRAFT: unweighted average slice constants do not control directional energy
entries.statement: Unreviewed independent counterexample: for each n>=2 let X be uniform on the covariance-identity regular simplex in sum-zero R^(n+1), with vertices sqrt((n+1)(n+2))(e_i-1/(n+1)). For u=(e_0-e_1)/sqrt(2), T=<X,u>, Y=X-Tu, and barycentric S=lambda_0+lambda_1, the conditional law of T is uniform of length sqrt(2(n+1)(n+2)) S. Set f=T(S-1/2)_+^2, a C1 function. Then E[f|Y]=0, partial_u f=(S-1/2)_+^2, and E Var(f|Y)/E|partial_u f|^2>(n+1)(n+2)/24, while mean conditional C_P=12/pi^2. Hence no universal directional conditional-variance bound follows by taking the unweighted average of slice constants. The valid slice estimate keeps C_P(T|Y) times conditional directional energy inside one expectation. Transverse derivatives and the conditional-mean variance require separate control in a full-gradient argument. This refutes only the stronger auxiliary bridge, not KLS; no novelty claim.
assumptions: n>=2; original Euclidean metric; conditional laws as in the stated simplex construction.
Only directional-u energy is used in the disproved bridge; full gradient energy is not being bounded or disproved.
Independent referee check pending; proof in ATTEMPT.md section 5.

relations.rationale: The displayed test ratio uses exactly the simplex fiber distribution, its affine S(Y), and conditional variance from the other entry.
